title: Different Christian readings of the 65 prophecy audits
scope: Informative Christian reception and disagreement, distinct from original ancient referent and independent event verification.
read_me_first: Interpretive schools are not denominational memberships. Catholic and Orthodox church sources support general typological approaches; Protestant authors disagree within denominations. Most linked framework sources document interpretive methods rather than offering page-specific endorsements of every illustrative example. Do not infer consensus or establish historical miracles from a later reading.

catholic_typology.label: Catholic Catechism §§128–130: typology and enduring original context
catholic_typology.scope: Official general hermeneutical framework, not a verse-by-verse ruling.

orthodox_typology.label: Orthodox Church in America: prophecy and Christ-centered interpretation
orthodox_typology.scope: Official catechetical overview, not a statement that every Orthodox reader agrees on a particular passage.

orthodox_scripture.label: Orthodox Church in America: How to Read the Bible
orthodox_scripture.scope: Representative Orthodox typological and liturgical methodology.

christian_apocalypse.label: Bible.org review of Steve Gregg's Four Views of Revelation book
christian_apocalypse.scope: Review of Steve Gregg's 1997 parallel-commentary book describing four interpretive approaches; not the book's full original arguments or a denomination-wide survey.

christians_fourviews.label: Probe Ministries: Four Views of Revelation
christians_fourviews.scope: Evangelical comparative overview of Revelation interpretation.

reformed_millennium.label: Ligonier (Reformed): The Millennial Maze
reformed_millennium.scope: Representative Reformed discussion of major millennial schools, not a uniform Protestant creed.

catholic_endtimes.label: Catholic Catechism §§675–677: last things and millenarianism
catholic_endtimes.scope: Official Catholic teaching rejects millenarianism while affirming a future final judgment.

adventist_daniel.label: Seventh-day Adventist General Conference: fundamental beliefs, heavenly sanctuary
adventist_daniel.scope: Official Seventh-day Adventist historicist reading of Daniel 8:14's 2,300-day period ending in 1844.

adventist_history.label: Adventist Church: 1844 and the Millerite interpretation
adventist_history.scope: Church self-history of the Daniel 8–9 calculation, the disappointment and subsequent teaching.

reformed_return.label: Ligonier (Reformed): The Return of Christ
reformed_return.scope: Representative Reformed distinction of first advent, second advent and prophetic fulfillment.

isaiah-7-14.label: Christological/typological (Catholic and Orthodox)
isaiah-7-14.explanation: Isaiah's sign to Ahaz retains its historical setting; Matthew reads the child/Immanuel motif through Jesus and Mary as a fuller Christ-centered sense.
isaiah-7-14.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

isaiah-7-14.label: Direct messianic prediction (some evangelicals)
isaiah-7-14.explanation: The verse is taken as an inspired prediction of Jesus' virginal conception, with Matthew's Greek citation governing the Christian interpretation.
isaiah-7-14.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

hosea-11-1.label: Recapitulation of Israel (Catholic and Orthodox typology)
hosea-11-1.explanation: Hosea narrates Israel's former Exodus; Matthew presents Jesus as reenacting Israel's history rather than quoting an isolated future-birth forecast.
hosea-11-1.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

hosea-11-1.label: Prophetic double significance (some evangelicals)
hosea-11-1.explanation: The Exodus statement is read as intentionally capable of a later messianic fulfillment in Jesus; this is a theological claim about Scripture's wider design.
hosea-11-1.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

jeremiah-31-15.label: Lament and typology
jeremiah-31-15.explanation: Rachel's grief over exile is treated as a type of the grief Matthew narrates in Bethlehem, even though Jeremiah originally anticipates a return.
jeremiah-31-15.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

jeremiah-31-15.label: Predictive messianic pattern
jeremiah-31-15.explanation: Some Christian readings treat Jeremiah's lament as a divinely foreseen echo of Herod's killing; Jeremiah itself does not name Herod.
jeremiah-31-15.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

micah-5-2.label: Messianic ruler with historical horizon
micah-5-2.explanation: Christian readings identify the ruler with Jesus, while retaining the oracle's original hope for a new Davidic leader in Judah's crisis.
micah-5-2.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

micah-5-2.label: Literal place-of-birth prediction
micah-5-2.explanation: A common evangelical argument treats Bethlehem as a specific advance prediction realized by the Gospel birth accounts; the independent birthplace evidence remains separate.
micah-5-2.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

zechariah-9-9.label: Jesus as humble king (liturgical/typological)

zechariah-9-9.label: Specific prediction fulfilled by entry details
zechariah-9-9.explanation: A predictive reading stresses the donkey and cheering crowd as intentionally forecast particulars; Gospel literary shaping remains a separate question.
zechariah-9-9.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

isaiah-53.label: Christ's passion as fulfillment (Catholic and Orthodox)

isaiah-53.explanation: The servant is understood as Jesus personally and in advance, including suffering for others' sins; the predictive interpretation requires an argument about Isaiah's original referent.
isaiah-53.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

psalm-22.label: Christological lament/typology
psalm-22.explanation: The psalm is an ancient lament prayed through Christ's crucifixion; its first-person suffering can be reread liturgically without proving every line was an isolated prediction.

psalm-22.label: Detailed passion prophecy
psalm-22.explanation: Other Christians emphasize pierced/hurt imagery, casting lots, and the crucifixion narratives as specific foretold facts; translation variants and quotation must be considered.
psalm-22.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

isaiah-40-3.label: New Exodus preparation

isaiah-40-3.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

ezekiel-29-egypt.label: Prophetic hyperbole and historical judgment

jonah-3-warning.attribution: illustrative Christian reading; NOT a verified denomination-wide position for this exact verse

nazorean-matthew-2-23.label: Thematic synthesis
